ticket.title: the suite view is a snapshot rather than a projection, so root reads serve stale member status and deleting the index changes the answer
ticket.description: Measured 2026-11-10 while closing SP-50, and it is why the board numbers in this session flip-flopped between two shapes. The root index (.gaugeblock/storypole/index.sqlite) held 374 task rows - a materialised copy of the whole suite - while storypole own index held 49 and the suite view answered 106 active. SP-50 was verified and archived in the storypole store, storypole show SP-50 in that store said Verified, and the root answered in_progress for the same ticket because its copy predates the verification. SP-47 and SP-49 read correctly in both, so the copy is refreshed by something that did not run after SP-50. Three measurements: (1) deleting workspace.sqlite changed nothing - the list still answered 106 rows with SP-50 in_progress, so the stale row is in index.sqlite; (2) deleting index.sqlite dropped the answer to 65 rows with SP-50 absent entirely, so the suite view is a snapshot rather than a projection rebuilt on read; (3) storypole ledger-reconcile reports index and ledger agree throughout, because it compares the root store own tasks and is blind to copied member rows. That falsifies the invariant SP-36 states - deleting index.sqlite changes no answer - for the suite view specifically. Consequence for the burn-down: every status read from the root may be stale by up to one rollup, so the owning repository is the only trustworthy reader, which is the opposite of what a meta-harness is for. Wanted: the suite view rebuilds from member records on read or on demand, a refresh verb that can be shown to converge, and reconcile extended to copied rows so a stale one is reported rather than agreed with. Acceptance: verifying a member ticket is visible from the root immediately, deleting either index file changes no answer, and reconcile names any row whose copy disagrees with its owner.
